newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up 12.96 pct at year high.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up 12.96 pct at year high.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index surged 8.641 points or 12.96 percent to end at a 1996 closing high of 75.331 points on Monday with investors buying heavily in low-priced stocks on bullish sentiment, traders said.
Volume was very heavy at 91.3 million shares, the biggest this year, valued at just under $34 million. All the 41 B shares traded today and all went up.

Traders said a bull run in the past three weeks sparked by expectations that Beijing will take measures to boost the market had greatly improved market sentiment and bargain-hunting in formerly less-fancied stocks helped push up the index.

"Despite the rises of the past three weeks, there are still big gaps between prices of Shanghai B shares compared with their A share or Shenzhen B share prices," one broker said. "The rising momentum is still strong."
"The index will jump further in the short term as most investors believe that it is worth investing in B shares," a second broker said.
Shanghai Lianhua Fibre was the star on bargain-hunting, surging $0.074 or 44.04 percent to $0.242, on volume of 3.6 million shares.
Shanghai Forever also rose on bargain-hunting, up $0.064 or 41.01 percent to $0.220, on volume of 8.1 million shares.
China Textile Machinery traded the most amid news that Sino-U.S. textile negotiations would continue, jumping $0.050 or 30.48 percent to $0.214, on volume of 12.0 million shares.
Shanghai A shares rose in active trading on bullish sentiment, brokers said.

The A index ended up 33.362 points or 2.62 percent to 1306.780 points, on volume of 1.4 billion shares worth 15.9 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index rose 80.175 points or 2.71 percent to 3038.236 points.
Taishan Tourism was the star on institutional buying, jumping 2.32 yuan or 17.76 percent to 15.38 yuan, on volume of 5.5 million shares.
